 JUDGMENT This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

sentences.text:
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 08-08-2022 at about 22:30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider on a two-wheeler bearing No.KA- 05-KW-3094, near NH-209 road, Harohalli Tank Band road, Harohalli Town, Harohalli Hobli, Ramanagara.

At that time, a concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations, came to extreme right side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Dr. Chandramma Dayananda Sagara Hospital, Devarakagalahalli, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.
Earlier to the accident he was working as a delivery boy in private company and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Harohalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Concrete Mixer Lorry for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

It has contended that, as on the date of accident, the rider of Honda Activa was not having valid and effective driving licence and he rode the same in rash and negligent manner, without following the traffic rules and regulations.

It has admitted that, it is the owner of Anshuman Raj vs Balaji Enterprises on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12513155/
2 the vehicle bearing No.KA- 53-D-2493 and having valid licence at the time of incident and the respondent No.2 was the insurer of the above said vehicle.
Hence, if at all there is any compensation awarded by this Court, then the liability may be shifted on the respondent No.2 herein.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the involvement of the concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 and also the manner of accident in the alleged accident.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties for the adjudication of the above petition.
The rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KW-3094, rode the same without wearing helmet and without holding valid and effective driving licence.
The pillion riders were also not wearing the helmet on the date of accident.
Further it is contended that, the owner and insurer of the concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 are not the necessary and proper parties for the adjudication of the above claim petition.
The owner of the motorcycle intentionally entrusted/allowed 3 adult persons to travel on the motorcycle on the road, knowing fully well that the seating capacity of the motorcycle is only 2.
The complaint, FIR, charge-sheet and other police documents clearly reflects that, at the time of accident three members were traveling on the motorcycle.
Hence, on this ground also above petition is liable to be dismissed as against the respondent No.2 insurance company.

Further it is contended that, the driver of the concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 was driving the same carefully, cautiously and on the correct side of the road, the accident in question took place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KW-3094 by its rider.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of concrete mixer lorry bearing No.KA-53-D-2493 and it was valid from 31-01-2022 to 30-01-2023.

It has contended that, the owner of the concrete mixer lorry bearing No.KA-53-D-2493 intentionally/willfully entrusted the vehicle to the person who did not had a valid and effective driving licence to drive the same on the date of the accident.
Hence, there is a breach and violations of the terms and conditions of the policy.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries,
medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KW-3094 has contributed to the cause of the accident and the degree of negligence on the part of the motorcycle was on the higher side, as such the liability if any, as far as this respondent is concerned should considerably be reduced and mitigated by taking into consideration of the higher degree of the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:

ISSUES Anshuman Raj vs Balaji Enterprises on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12513155/
3

1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 08-08-2022 at about 22:30 p.m., near NH-209 road, Harohalli Tank Band Road, Harohalli Town, Harohalli Hobli,
Ramanagara, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Concrete Mixer Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA- 53-D-2493 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
7. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Further, he has got examined two more witnesses namely Siddesh K.M.
and Dr. Nagaraj B.N., as P.W.2 and P.W.3 respectively.
On the other hand, the respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 08-08-2022 at about 22:30 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider on a two-wheeler bearing No.KA- 05-KW-3094, near NH-209 road, Harohalli Tank Band road, Harohalli Town, Harohalli Hobli, Ramanagara, the offending concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations, came to extreme right side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident he was working as a delivery boy in private company and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazer, Ex.P.4 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.6 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.8 are medical bills (total 45), Ex.P.9 are prescriptions (total 5), Ex.P.10 is Anshuman Raj vs Balaji Enterprises on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12513155/
4 notarized copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.11 are x-rays (total 3), Ex.P.12 is authorization letter, Ex.P.13 is in-patient record, Ex.P.14 is true copy of MLC Register extract, Ex.P.15 are x- rays, Ex.P.16 is discharge summary, Ex.P.17 is clinical notes and Ex.P.18 is x-ray.

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner, while he was proceeding as a pillion rider on said motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KW-3094, near NH-209 road, Harohalli Tank Band road, Harohalli Town, Harohalli Hobli, Ramanagara.
Further it reveals that, in the said accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injury on his left leg and simple injuries on the other parts of the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.7, has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

13. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the involvement of concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53- D-2493 in the alleged accident, the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2, in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

The respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KW-3094 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

They have neither adduced any evidence to establish the above contentions, nor they have produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in their written statements on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner from opposite direction.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle or there was any contributory negligence on his part, in the cause of accident.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestions made in his cross-examination that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-53-D-2493.
14.

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place at the middle of 22 feet wide Kanakapura-Bengaluru NH-209 road, Harohalli Tank Band road, Harohalli Town, Harohalli Hobli, Ramanagara, in between the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KW-3094 and offending concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493.

Further,
as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken Anshuman Raj vs Balaji Enterprises on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12513155/
5 place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

sentences.text: When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the respondents have not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the said documents are false and concocted documents.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence on record to show that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg.

. In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. But, it is pertinent to note that, admittedly, at the time of accident the petitioner and two others were triple riders on the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KW-3094.

This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner consciously and being fully aware that, triple riding is not allowed and it amounts to violation of the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act and it may lead the rider to lose control over the said vehicle due to congestion, has taken risk of traveling on the said motorcycle as a pillion rider.
No doubt, mere act of triple riding does not amount to contributory negligence.
But, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case the pillion riders were not the children, but, they are young and healthy persons, both aged about 19 years respectively.

In such circumstances, there are every chances that, due to triple riding on the motorcycle by the petitioner, which is meant for two persons, there would have been congestion to the rider of motorcycle and he might have lost control and contributed in the cause of accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident has taken place just beside the middle line of the road.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the very act of triple riding by the petitioner has also contributed in the cause of accident to some extent.

But, as there is no cogent and corroborative evidence to show that, the very act of triple riding has contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the petitioner is liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% would meet the ends of justice.

16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.11 x-rays (total 3),
Ex.P.13 in-patient record, Ex.P.15 x-ray, Ex.P.16 discharge summary, Ex.P.17 clinical notes and Ex.P.18 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury in a road traffic accident i.e. fracture shaft of the left femur.

The P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

On the other hand, there is no rebuttal Anshuman Raj vs Balaji Enterprises on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12513155/
6 evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.
17.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
18.

entities.text: Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
19. Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 08-08-2022 at about 22:30 p.m., near NH-209 road, Harohalli Tank Band Road, Harohalli Town, Harohalli Hobli,
Ramanagara, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493.
But, the petitioner has failed to prove that, the said accident has taken place due to sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending concrete mixer lorry.
There is contributory negligence even on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident, to the extent of 10%.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained fracture shaft of the left femur.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e.
pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10, the date of birth of the petitioner is 08-07-2003.
The accident has taken place on 08-08-2022 at about 10.30 p.m.
This clearly goes show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 19 years.
Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability,

has clearly deposed in his Anshuman Raj vs Balaji Enterprises on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12513155/
7 examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture shaft of the left femur and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 47% to the left lower limb and 16% to the whole body.

Further, the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.11 x-rays (total 3), Ex.P.13 inpatient record, Ex.P.15 x-ray, Ex.P.16 discharge summary, Ex.P.17 clinical notes and Ex.P.18 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 08-08-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 30-01-2024,
which is after lapse of one year and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fracture sustained by the petitioner is united.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10%
to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10%
to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as a delivery boy in a private company and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.

Further, he has deposed that,
due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as a delivery boy in a private company and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 19 years is 18.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 10/100 X 18 = Rs.3,34,800/-.

8 ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 45 medical bills, as per Ex.P.8.

iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
fracture shaft of the left femur.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

As per Ex.P.16 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 28 days in Dr. Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Institute of Medical Education and Research, Harohalli.

Bihar State, the accident has taken place near NH-209 road, Harohalli Tank Band Road, Harohalli Town, Harohalli Hobli, Ramanagara and the petitioner has taken treatment at Dr. Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Institute of Medical Education and Research, Harohalli.

Harohalli, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.

viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 19 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture shaft of the left femur.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.

Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and Anshuman Raj vs Balaji Enterprises on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12513155/
9 reasonable.
ix)
Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.3 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs. 5,49,834-00 90% of Total Rs.
4,94,850-60

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,94,851/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
22. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-53-D-2493.
It is not in dispute that, the policy issued by the respondent No.2 bearing No.VOC0622614000100, in respect of offending concrete mixer lorry was valid from 31-01-2022 to 30-01-2023.
The said policy was valid as on the date of accident.
But, the respondent No.2 has taken specific contention that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
In this regard it has examined its representative/Manager as R.W.1.

The R.W.1 has filed his examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has deposed that, the owner of the vehicle has willfully entrusted the offending concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D- 2493 to a person who did not held a valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of the accident,
in violation of Section 3(1) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further he has deposed that, the Company Investigator visited the Police Station to collect information and documents and he collected all the documents and copy of driving licence of Jitu Gowola S/o Mojesh Gowala and the insurance Anshuman Raj vs Balaji Enterprises on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12513155/

10 company has sent the same to concerned RTO for verification, for which they have issued a letter stating that, the driving licence in the name of Jitu Gowola S/o Mojesh Gowala is not correct/genuine one.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to indemnify the insured/owner of the concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493, as he has committed breach of terms and conditions of policy.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against the respondent No.2.
Further, he has produced certified copy of information letter dated 25-05-2023, issued by Regional Transport Officer, Motor Vehicle Department, Nagaland.

23. As per the information provided under Ex.R.3 letter, issued by the R.T.O., Mokokchung,
Nagaland, the driving licence bearing No. NL-0220190077479, is not issued by the said R.T.O.,
Mokokchung, Nagaland and it is stated that, the same may be treated as false and fabricated driving licence.

In such circumstances, the burden was on the respondent No.1 to rebut the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2, by producing the original driving licence of his driver by name Jitu Gowala S/o Mojesh Gowala or by examining the said licence holder.

But, the respondent No.1 did not care to produce the original driving licence of his driver or to examine his driver, to establish that as on the date of accident his driver was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Even, the respondent No.1 has not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in his written statement on oath.
As such, the respondent No.1 has failed to discharge his burden.

Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to hold that, the respondent No.1 has failed to prove that, the driver of offending concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident.

As such there is breach of fundamental terms and conditions of Ex.R.2 policy issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493.
24.

The learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently argued that, the drive of offending lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident an as there is breach of fundamental condition of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1, the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, for any liability or compensation awarded by this Court.

In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has relied on the following decisions of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka:
i) Smt. Adilakshmammama and others V/s Raju B. and another, in MFA No.3297/2019 (MV-D), dated 13-04-2023.
ii) M/s. Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Mrs. Sunitha @ Nagaveni and others, in MFA No.4716/2011 (MV), dated 12-01- 2016.
iii) Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi W/o Renukappa V/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.
Ltd., and another, in MFA No.6154/2019 (MV-D), dated 14-12-2023.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, it is settled principle of law that, even if there is a fundamental breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act, the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover the same from the insured.

26. For the reasons stated supra, the respondent No.1 has failed to prove that, the driver of offending offending concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident.

Further, it is not the case of the respondent No.1 that, he was not having knowledge that, his driver was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle or he was not having knowledge that, the licence held by his driver was a fake licence.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to hold that, the respondent No.1/owner of offending vehicle was having knowledge that, the driver of offending offending lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident and consciously he had handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess driving licence.

In such circumstances,
this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2)
of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further, as the accident in question has taken place after the date of coming into force of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner that, even if there is a fundamental breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act, the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover the same from the insured, does not hold good.

As such, the arguments advanced by learned counsel for respondent No.2 and the ratio laid down in the above cited judgments relied by him are aptly applicable to the present facts and circumstances of the case.

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions, this Court is of the considered opinion that, as there is breach of fundamental terms and condition of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1, in respect of offending concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Accordingly, holding that the respondent No.1 being the owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay the above compensation amount Rs.4,94,851/- to the petitioner, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,94,851/- (Rupees four lakh ninety four thousand eight hundred and fifty one only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 is held liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and he is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the respondents have not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the said documents are false and concocted documents.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence on record to show that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
. In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner consciously and being fully aware that, triple riding is not allowed and it amounts to violation of the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act and it may lead the rider to lose control over the said vehicle due to congestion, has taken risk of traveling on the said motorcycle as a pillion rider.
No doubt, mere act of triple riding does not amount to contributory negligence.
But, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case the pillion riders were not the children, but, they are young and healthy persons, both aged about 19 years respectively.
In such circumstances, there are every chances that, due to triple riding on the motorcycle by the petitioner, which is meant for two persons, there would have been congestion to the rider of motorcycle and he might have lost control and contributed in the cause of accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the very act of triple riding by the petitioner has also contributed in the cause of accident to some extent.
But, as there is no cogent and corroborative evidence to show that, the very act of triple riding has contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the petitioner is liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% would meet the ends of justice.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
18.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10%
to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10%
to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as a delivery boy in a private company and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.
As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 19 years is 18.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the respondent No.1 to rebut the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2, by producing the original driving licence of his driver by name Jitu Gowala S/o Mojesh Gowala or by examining the said licence holder.
But, the respondent No.1 did not care to produce the original driving licence of his driver or to examine his driver, to establish that as on the date of accident his driver was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to hold that, the respondent No.1 has failed to prove that, the driver of offending concrete mixer lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident.
As such there is breach of fundamental terms and conditions of Ex.R.2 policy issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-2493.
